This is my first visit to Rouge National Urban Park, and I must say that this trail is a gem for those residing in the Greater Toronto Area. It offers stunning natural vistas with a moderate level of effort, all conveniently reachable by a short drive. The trail guides you through a diverse range of landscapes, treating hikers to various captivating viewpoints. For individuals reasonably fit, this hike presents no significant challenge and can be comfortably finished within 1.5 to 2 hours, allowing ample time to savour the surrounding scenery. However, while undeniably beautiful, it didn't quite deliver an exceptionally thrilling experience, which is its only minor drawback.

Due to time constraints, I had the opportunity to explore only this particular trail, but I look forward to returning and exploring the other trails that this park has to offer. Especially with the vibrant fall foliage on the horizon.

A pleasant and accessible hike up the Little Rough River that I’ve done a few times in the off season.  The walk from the parking lot to the trail head up the road is usually crowded regardless.  The trail isn’t as busy though. It starts by a pond that has lots of migratory birds and ducks. We saw numerous turtles sunning themselves too.  The trail then takes you to the top of the valley, down to the river and into a beautiful cedar forest. Plenty of old growth trees too. Be warned this entire area is tick infested. Wear appropriate clothes and check your dog well. We pulled a half dozen off our pup.

I can’t believe I missed this trail! I’ve spent hours and hours on All Trails and have hiked The Rouge before but I never knew this 8km trail existed. When I got there the trail was across the road from the parking lot. It seemed like no one knew it existed. And for most the hike there was no one to be seen. So hard to believe because the Rouge is typically a very busy trail. Seemed like I had found a diamond in the rough. The trail was spectacular. It had all the views of the main Rouge trails with the added bonus of some amazing river views along the way. I even found a road that doesn’t show up on the trail map. I’m super excited to go back and explore it. The hike took me about 4 hours but that’s because I took a half hour break in my hammock with some snacks. The weather was perfect and the conditions were great. The trail was pretty dry for the most part. There is a view from the top of the bluffs that’s off of the main trail a bit but totally worth checking out. My picture does not do it justice. It’s breathtaking. I’ll be back soon to try out the hidden trail! 10/10

AVOID THIS PLACE! My wife, our dog and I went for a hike on this trail on October 24th, 2021. We hiked this trail as well as the Vista Trail. We never went off-trail, the dog was leashed the whole time, and we were out there for approximately two hours. When we got home we found 11 (yes, ELEVEN) ticks between the three of us. I wrote the park to let them know, and they replied to note that there is a warning sign at the trail head (there is!), and to say that public health officials don't really monitor tick numbers anymore because, well, there are too many of them lol. FIND ANOTHER PLACE TO HIKE! This place is beyond infested...

*Don't go to parking coordinate there is no parking there.  You'll need to park near the Vista Trail head off of Zoo Road 43°49'05.8"N 79°10'21.7"W there is parallel side of road parking during the off season.  But not available during the summer months (read signs carefully).  From there choose your hike as a number of trails connect from here.  Park maps: http://www.rvcc.ca/Rouge_Park_Hiking_Trails.html

Also it can be pretty noisy in sections due to traffic.  Hope that helps!

Great trail but doesn’t make sense that there is no parking at the north end, especially with all that land, not thought out well whatsoever to be inviting. That being said a great hike whether you want to do the whole thing or just half with young kids.

Nice trail, easy to navigate and level easy terrain. A couple of small hills throughout but completely manageable. This trail can be connected to many other trails south of Twyn Rivers Drive (all part of the same park) south of Twyn Rivers is much prettier scenery and takes you through more forested areas. Trail got fairly busy by about 9:30am on a Sunday. Also there is NO parking to enter the Cedar Trail at the north end, off of Morningside, the only place to park is on the south end off of Twyn Rivers Drive (there is a parking lot) Also NOTE: there were lots of black legged ticks in early December. We had to pick them off ourselves and the dogs.
My dog and I loved this trail. The whole rouge valley actually is just a great place to be outside! Definitely will do again!

Very nice trail. The only problem was the lack of parking. We had to park on the side of the road.

Beautiful trail, not very challenging, but very beautiful and interesting. Great views, some ascents and descents, lots of wildflowers. Great trail for birdwatching--May is prime time to spot warblers (I've seen yellow and chestnut-sided in past years), rose-breasted grosbeaks, and more. Winter, look for gold and ruby crowned kinglets.
I really enjoy this trail and have been hiking it for years. One of my favourites in the Rouge.

Trail running. First time at this park. Went for a 9 mile run. Overall it was a good trail. It did get a little confusing a couple of times with all of the smaller trails that branch off without any markings. I wanted to find something with soft surface where I could get a decent number of miles, so it worked perfect for that.

It was a good park to have a fairly easy walk on, with only a few steep hills. The only negatives I had were the lack of consistent trail markers and the relatively boring scenery after we left the creek. We ended up getting lost because the trail markers petered out and there were lots of side trails, and the middle section was just rough gravel. Nice and long, with places to loop around if you want a shorter walk. Dogs are on leash only. There is only street parking.
